No View Is the Whole

A Second-Order Philosophy of Understanding, Action, and Revision

Soman Lin

A computer alarm appears as Eagle descends towards the Moon. The crew needs a decision before anyone has a complete explanation. Everyday life poses quieter versions of the same difficulty: how can we act, predict, and understand ourselves while our knowledge remains unfinished?

This book develops a second-order framework for examining how questions, representations, methods, and purposes fit together. Its concern is what understanding enables us to do, under which conditions, and at whose expense. The framework also turns those questions on itself.

Fifteen chapters in four parts, seventeen images, and seventy-nine source notes. Complete Chinese and English editions, switchable inside the reader.

所見非全貌

理解、行動與修正的二階哲學

Soman Lin

鷹號正向月面下降，導引電腦卻亮起警報。原因尚未查清，太空人已需要一個決定。日常生活也有這樣的難題：理解還不完整，我們仍須預測環境、認識自己，並採取行動。

本書從具體案例逐步建立一套二階框架，回看問題如何形成、表示留下什麼、方法依賴哪些條件，以及目的能否重新考慮。它關心理解有什麼用，也追問對誰有用、代價由誰承擔，最後把同樣的問題問向自己。

全書十五章分成四部，十七張圖、七十九項來源註釋。中英文全文可在閱讀器內切換。
